headline: Designing beyond trends, dressing for the memory.
bioParagraphs: I started Adora Fashions with a single machine, a borrowed table and a stubborn belief: that a woman should never have to choose between being beautifully dressed and being herself. Nine years later that belief still runs the studio. Every commission begins with a conversation, not a catalogue.

My work sits deliberately between African tradition and modern tailoring. I drape, I cut by hand, I fit on the body three times before a single stitch is finished. Traditional pieces carry the weight of the cloth they are made from; contemporary pieces are built to be worn, washed, lived in and repaired — not archived after one evening.

The atelier is deliberately small. It means you work with me, from first sketch to final pressing. It also means the calendar fills. I take a limited number of commissions each season so that every name on my rail gets the attention it deserves.
pullQuote: A dress is not something you wear. It is something that remembers you, and keeps remembering long after the evening ends.

philosophy.label: Fabric
philosophy.detail: Sourced in small lots from weavers and mills we have worked with for years. Cloth is chosen for how it will age, not just how it photographs.

philosophy.label: Fit
philosophy.detail: Three fittings, blocked by hand on the body. Nothing is graded down from a master size — the pattern is drafted to you.

philosophy.label: Finish
philosophy.detail: French seams, hand-finished hems, set-in sleeves. The parts your eye never catches are the parts we spend longest on.
